samples.summary: stampLens's "fill blanks only" rule lets a FRESH model-supplied `lens` field survive, re-opening the origin-spoofing hole prior-findings.mjs closes by overwriting
samples.evidence: `stampLens` (review-panel.mjs:815) only assigns when `typeof f.lens !== "string"`. The justification (line 804-806, and 2478-2479 in main) is that `priorForLens` is already filtered to `p.lens === lens.id` — true for PRIOR findings, but the other input to `merged` is `kept`, i.e. this round's raw model output. FINDING (line 79-111) declares no `additionalProperties: false` and `coerceFindings` (line 531-535) passes objects through untouched, so a lens that emits `{"lens":"docs", ...}` keeps it. Matching is lens-only-scoped: `rebuttals` in main() is the GLOBAL list (line 2177-2186), never filtered per lens, and `matchRebuttal` gates purely on `findingSimilarity`'s `trimmed(a.lens) !== trimmed(b.lens)` (rounds.mjs:303). So a mis-tagged fresh finding either (a) can be matched against another lens's rebuttal and overturned off the gate, or (b) can never match its own lens's rebuttal. The repo already states this exact hazard and resolves it the other way: prior-findings.mjs:104-106 puts `lens` LAST with the comment "a finding cannot spoof its own origin by carrying a `lens` key, since these come from a previous round's model output." An unconditional stamp here is strictly safe (every prior entry already equals `lens.id`). Sub-case: a fresh finding emitting `lens: ""` is treated as already-stamped and silently keeps the pre-fix inert behaviour.

samples.summary: The stated identity rationale for "blanks only" is factually wrong — unconditional copying would NOT break `overturnedOut.has(f)` removal
samples.evidence: review-panel.mjs:798-802 (and the mirrored comment at 2471-2477) claims "Returning fresh copies unconditionally would leave every overturned finding un-removable from the summary". That is false: `const merged = stampLens(...)` (line 2480) stores the copies themselves, `gatingRaw = gatingFindings(merged)` filters without copying (line 830), `adjudged.dropped` holds those same objects (line 1967), and `merged.filter((f) => !overturnedOut.has(f))` (line 2506) therefore still matches. Only the "stamp here, not on gatingRaw" half of the argument is load-bearing. The wrong half is what motivates the never-overwrite rule flagged above, so the incorrect comment is actively steering a behavioural decision.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the working tree. stampLens (review-panel.mjs:815) fills only blank `lens` values, and its stated justification ("priorForLens is already filtered to p.lens === lens.id", lines 804-806 / 2478-2479) covers only one of the two inputs to `merged` — the other is `kept`, this round's raw model output (2480). The FINDING schema (79-111) omits `additionalProperties: false` and is passed verbatim to the SDK as json_schema output (ask.mjs:463, review-panel.mjs:1667), so a model-emitted `lens` key is schema-legal; coerceFindings returns well-formed findings untouched (531-535), clusterFindings keeps the ORIGINAL member objects while only comparing lens-neutral copies (629-644, mergeCluster 656), so the key survives to gating. Matching is not lens-scoped: `rebuttals` is a single global list (2177-2186) handed unfiltered to adjudicateRebuttals (2492), which calls matchRebuttal(f, rebuttals) per finding with no lens filter (1953) and can drop the finding on an overturn (1965-1968); findingSimilarity's only lens rule is the equality test at rounds.mjs:303. Consequence is exactly as claimed: a mis-tagged fresh finding can be matched to a foreign lens's rebuttal and overturned off the gate, or can never match its own lens's rebuttal (including the `lens: ""` sub-case, which 815 treats as already-stamped). The repo already recognizes this hazard and resolves it by unconditional overwrite at prior-findings.mjs:104-106. No guard, caller-side filter, or field whitelist makes the path unreachable, and the impact (lost blocker / inert adjudication loop) is in the correctness lane.
